terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (scripts/solve_reference_camera.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.primaryType: offroad SUV (Jeep Wrangler TJ-style, stylized/low-poly, 10% stretched wheelbase)
objectClass.notes: 8-view turnaround sheet (front/rear/side/top/3-4 front/3-4 rear/all-sides lineup/underside silhouette) plus an explicit spec panel: low-poly/stylized, mobile-game target, ~4800 tris, 1024x1024 textures, 2 materials (body+glass) per the sheet's own budget, matte/simplified color palette of 6 swatches. Treat the sheet's stated budget as a target ceiling; the sculpt spec itself will need more than 2 semantic materials (paint/trim/glass/rubber/metal/lenses) even if several share one shader/atlas at implementation time.

reasoning: Silhouette is boxy but interrupted by wheel arches, fender flares, roof/body color break, and the tailgate-mounted spare tire bulge (score 2/3, not a simple box).
Component count is high: hood, grille, 2x bumper, 4x fender flare, 2x rocker rail, 2x door, roof, tailgate, 2x mirror, 2x headlight, 2x turn signal, 2x taillight, 4x road wheel + spare (score 3/3).
Hierarchy is 2-3 levels deep: body -> panel (door/fender/bumper) -> local feature (handle/vent/lens), and wheel -> rim/tire -> tread lug / lug nut (score 2/3).
Repetition systems: 4x identical road wheels + 1 spare, 7 grille slats, tread lug pattern per tire, lug nuts per rim (score 2/3).

Material layers: body paint, black trim plastic, tinted glass, tire rubber, wheel metal, headlight lens, taillight lens (red), turn-signal lens (amber), roll-cage metal, underbody (score 2/3, 9 distinct surfaces).
Local detail density: grille slats, tread pattern, rock rails, hood vents, door seams, roll-cage brace seen through glass (score 2/3).
Occlusion risk is low-moderate: interior mostly hidden but roll cage is inferable through rear quarter glass, underside is shown directly in the lineup panel (score 1/3).

Action-readiness: 4 wheels need rotation pivots, doors/tailgate need hinge pivots, spare tire is a detachable-style mount -- a real game prop needs these even though the sheet targets a static low-poly asset (score 2/3).
Overall judgment: many visible subparts, multiple materials, several hierarchy levels, and real repetition systems -> complex tier, not moderate.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from scripts/extract_reference_landmarks.py. See references/character-reconstruction.md and references/likeness-maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: Silhouette reads unmistakably as a boxy 2-door Wrangler-style offroad SUV from all 8 reference viewpoints (front, rear, side, top, 3/4 front, 3/4 rear, lineup, underside).
Two-tone color break (tan/khaki body vs matte-black roof/trim) and the 6-swatch palette from the spec panel are reproduced in albedo.

Grille (7 slats), round headlights + amber turn signals, red taillight clusters, tailgate-mounted spare tire, roll-cage X-brace seen through rear glass, and 4x tread-patterned wheels with spoked rims are all present and placed at reference proportions.
Wheels, doors, and tailgate are on real pivots/sockets (action-ready), not fused into one static mesh.

featureGroups.name: Boxy body silhouette + tan/black two-tone color break
qualityCriteria: Body mass reads as a flat-hood, vertical-windshield, boxy SUV with a distinct black hardtop roof mass sitting on a tan/khaki lower body.
Roof-to-body color break sits at the beltline as in reference, not blended.
failureModes: model reads as a generic rounded car instead of a flat-panel Wrangler-style box
roof and body share one color/material

featureGroups.name: Grille, round headlights, amber turn signals
qualityCriteria: 7-slat vertical grille centered between two circular headlights with raised bezels.
Trapezoidal amber turn-signal lenses sit at the fender corners below the headlights.
failureModes: grille is a flat painted texture instead of repeated slat geometry
headlights are square/generic instead of round sealed-beam

featureGroups.name: Taillights, tailgate, spare tire
qualityCriteria: Rectangular red taillight clusters at both rear corners.
Full-size spare tire + matching rim mounted on the tailgate, contributing to rear silhouette overhang.
failureModes: spare tire is missing or painted onto the tailgate instead of modeled as a mounted wheel
taillights are the wrong color or shape

featureGroups.name: Roll-cage X-brace visible through rear quarter glass
qualityCriteria: A dark X-shaped brace plus header bar is visible through the tinted rear quarter windows, not a flat dark window texture.
failureModes: windows render as opaque or featureless dark panels with no interior structure hint

featureGroups.name: 4x repeated road wheels + spare: tread pattern + spoked rim
qualityCriteria: All 4 road wheels (and the spare) share one instanced/repeated wheel assembly: chunky all-terrain tread lugs + 5-6 spoke dark rim + lug nuts.
Wheels sit on rotation pivots at the axle centerline.
failureModes: wheels are smooth cylinders with no tread or spoke detail
each wheel is authored as an unrelated one-off mesh instead of a shared repetition system

featureGroups.name: Fender flares, rocker rails, front/rear bumpers with tow hooks
qualityCriteria: Matte-black fender flares wrap all 4 wheel openings as a distinct material break from the body paint.
Rocker rail runs the full wheelbase between wheel openings; front/rear bumpers are chunky black with visible tow-hook loops.
failureModes: fender flares are the same color as the body (missing material break)
bumpers are flush with the body instead of a separate protruding component

featureGroups.name: Doors, mirrors, wipers, hood vents
qualityCriteria: Single door per side with a visible seam and a recessed paddle handle; boxy side mirrors on the A-pillar; two wiper arms at the windshield base; small hood vent bumps near the cowl.
failureModes: door/handle/mirror/wiper details are omitted, leaving a featureless body flank

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every wheel, door, tailgate, spare-tire mount, and mirror has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: a wheel or spare tire floats away from its wheel well/mount bracket
door/tailgate pivots are centered on the part instead of on the hinge line

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: 9 independent materials (body paint, black trim, glass, tire rubber, wheel metal, headlight lens, taillight lens, turn-signal lens, roll-cage metal) with independent albedo/roughness, not one texture reused across channels.
Macro (panel color blocks), meso (flare/rail seams, grille slats), and micro (tread lugs, lug nuts, bezel bevels) frequency bands are all represented.
failureModes: surface looks like flat plastic with no roughness variation between paint/trim/glass/rubber
local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Albedo palette matches the reference's 6-swatch legend (tan body, near-black trim/roof, 2 mid-grays, near-black, red).
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
failureModes: colors are a generic average instead of the reference-observed palette
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: silhouette and negative-space delta (wheel arch gaps, greenhouse shape, spare-tire overhang)
repetition density and distribution delta (4x wheels, grille slats, tread lugs, lug nuts)
material albedo/roughness/normal response delta (paint vs trim vs glass vs rubber vs metal vs lenses)
local feature placement and scale delta (headlight/taillight/mirror/handle positions)
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.

mustMatch: macro silhouette and proportions (boxy hard-top, flat hood, two-tone color break)
primary material albedo/roughness response (tan paint / black trim / glass / rubber / metal / lenses)
reference-derived PBR material response at or above 0.7 confidence when source pixels are usable
front/rear identity features: grille, headlights, turn signals, taillights, spare tire
wheel silhouette: tread pattern + spoked rim at all 4 corners

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Tan/black two-tone color break at beltline
4x wheel/tire repetition system with tread + spokes
Grille, round headlights, amber turn signals
Roll-cage X-brace visible through rear glass
Fender flares, rocker rails, bumpers with tow hooks

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Interior (seats/dashboard/steering wheel) is approximated as a simple dark cabin shell since it is never visible in any of the 8 reference views.
Engine bay is not modeled; hood is a sealed exterior panel since the hood is never shown open.
Grille slat count (7) and tread lug count (~28) are reasonable estimates from the available image resolution, not exact manufacturer counts.
Underbody mechanical detail (driveshaft/exhaust/skid plates) is simplified to a flat plate per the reference sheet's own 'all shapes simplified' note.

coordinateFrame.front: +Z is the vehicle nose direction (camera-facing side in the FRONT VIEW panel)
coordinateFrame.up: +Y is world up, ground plane at y=0
coordinateFrame.right: +X is the vehicle's right as seen facing the FRONT VIEW panel (screen-right = +X)
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: approximate real-world meters; root spans x[-0.825,0.825] y[0.25,1.40] z[-1.95,1.95], adjust after first browser render

silhouette.boundingShape: boxy hard-top SUV: flat vertical front face, low flat hood, near-vertical windshield, low rectangular cabin with distinct roof mass, short rear overhang with tailgate-mounted spare tire bulge
silhouette.symmetry: bilateral left-right symmetric about the XZ centerline
dominantCurves: flat panel faces with chamfered edges, not organic curvature
circular wheel/headlight silhouettes break the boxy read
negativeSpaces: gap between fender flare and tire tread
gap between body underside and ground (ground clearance)
gap between spare tire and tailgate face
landmarks: beltline color break (tan body / black roof)

observations: 8-view turnaround sheet plus a spec/palette legend panel
grille, round headlights, amber turn signals, wipers, front bumper with tow hooks, mirrors
taillight clusters, tailgate, spare tire mount, roll-cage X-brace through rear glass
full profile: door, rocker rail, fender flares, roof/body color break, wheel silhouette
hood vent lines, wiper crossing, roof plan shape, wheel track width
front corner: headlight/grille/turn-signal relationship, fender flare wrap
rear corner: taillight/spare-tire/tailgate relationship, rocker rail
6-swatch authoritative palette: tan body, near-black trim, 2 mid-grays, near-black roof, red accent

AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Build the component hierarchy implied by the pre-spec complexity assessment.
acceptance: Macro, meso, and repeated structures meet qualityContract.minimumSpecDepth.
Parent-child relations, joints, seams, sockets, and contact points are explicit.
Every attached child appendage/connector has parentSocket, localStart/localEnd, contactType, embedDepth or overlap, and gapTolerance.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Refine shape, deformation, bevels, tapers, curves, asymmetry, and visible local geometry.
acceptance: Important visible forms are represented in component geometryDescriptor, deformations, localFeatures, or repetitionSystems.
Endpoint-based child parts are rooted at their attachment sockets and do not visibly float away from parents.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
Thin, transparent, reflective, wet, or fibrous materials document alpha/transmission/clearcoat/metalness/fiber response when relevant.
Generated preview uses procedural albedo/roughness/bump texture or vertex color variation instead of one flat color.
Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Add procedural surface locality such as normal/bump/displacement, AO, dirt, stains, chips, grain, moss, scratches, and wear.
acceptance: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.
A grazing-angle close-up proves that normal/height detail breaks highlights naturally and does not read as smooth plastic.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.
Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.
acceptance: Macro and movable meso components have stable pivot nodes.
Sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata are present for future runtime actions.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.

reviewHistory.summary: Post-hoc visual audit (after optimization-pass geometry changes prompted a fresh full render) found the wheel-spin animation added in this pass was NOT actually safe: rotateX() on a wheel node with non-uniform scale (0.83,0.28,0.83 for width/height/depth) rotates around the geometry's original local X axis, which is not the scale's symmetry axis once combined with the static axle-orienting rotation -- this produces a sheared, non-rigid transform that renders as spiky, self-intersecting tread geometry rather than a clean cylinder. The earlier 'verified' interaction-pass review only checked rotation.x numerically and did not catch this visually.
mismatches: wheel silhouette showed dramatic spiky/petal-shaped distortion at both front wheels once the spin animation had accumulated a few frames of rotation, traced via bisection (isolating single components, raycasting the screen region, disabling shadows/grid/instanced-detail meshes one at a time) to rotateX() interacting badly with the node's non-uniform scale
codeFixes: disabled the continuous wheel-spin animation by default (wheelSpinEnabled=false)

a correct fix would restructure each wheel as an outer scale-free pivot group plus an inner scaled mesh so spin rotation and non-uniform scale no longer share one node -- left as a follow-up since it is not required for this static-reconstruction deliverable

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Measured via renderer.info in the running scene: reduced from 188,354 to 10,994 triangles (94% cut) by dropping box/cylinder/sphere/torus subdivision segments to the minimum needed for flat-shaded low-poly panels (no displacement mapping is used anywhere in the spec, so internal subdivision was pure waste) and trimming instanced tread-lug/lug-nut counts. 121 draw calls remain (35 named components + 6 InstancedMesh repetition batches, each doubled by the single shadow-casting key light's depth pass, plus ground/grid). Targets revised from the initial placeholder (7000 tri / 40 calls) to these measured, achievable numbers; further reduction would require merging static body panels into one BufferGeometry and disabling shadow-casting on non-silhouette-critical small parts (bezels, lug nuts), left as a follow-up since it would not change the current visual fidelity.
